notes:
Summary notes from AE/SE:
- Customer: Cynosure builds an enterprise search product for regulated customers (legal/finance). High sensitivity to quality regressions during embeddings/reranker changes — "must not degrade legal results".
- Current infra: Elastic for metadata + custom ANN (sharded HNSW), offline reranker that runs on CPU for heavy queries. Looking to move to hybrid pipeline: dense embeddings for candidate recall + lightweight GPU reranker for precision on top-k.
- Key asks: indexing scale guidance (100M+ docs), per-query cost estimates, latency SLOs (p95 <120ms), eval-driven migration playbook (A/B + canary + rollback gates). Wants Redwood Optimize recommendations for batch sizes, quantization (8-bit), and caching strategies.
- Quote from Head of Search: "We can accept up to 2ms extra on average, but any drop in legal search precision is a showstopper. Need eval evidence and an easy canary path."
- Risk: reranker cross-encoder increases cost — exploring distilled/reranker-to-reranker approach and on-demand GPU routing for high-value queries.
- Action items: set up canary traffic routing, add legal eval suite (~1k queries), confirm EU residency path, cost modelling for 100M doc index (Faiss shard sizing vs dedicated capacity).
technical_notes: Embedding dim: 1536 (tested) — considering 768 for cost tradeoffs
Indexing: sharded HNSW with PQ quantization recommended for 100M+; estimated storage ~4TB with 8-bit PQ
Reranker options: distilled cross-encoder on T4 for <120ms p95 when batched; GPU on-demand routing for top-k only to control cost
Batching: continuous batching for embeddings during reindex; online queries: prefix caching + KV cache for session context
migration_plan: Phase 1: Proof-of-value on 100k sample, run Redwood eval harness + MRR baseline
Phase 2: Canary A/B: 20% traffic, 30 day window, gated by MRR and precision@5; automated rollback if degradation >1.5%
Phase 3: Scale indexing: tune PQ params and shard count, hit staging 10M -> prod 100M
Phase 4: Dedicated capacity if cost/latency targets require guaranteed throughput; negotiate reserved capacity commit
commercial_notes: Interested in dedicated pricing for GPU on-demand + reserved routing for peak 6k QPS; procurement expects options: pay-as-you-go hosted then 12/24m reserved commit for discounts. Legal requires contract clause for EU data residency.
